newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean traders seen seeking more Argentine corn.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean traders seen seeking more Argentine corn.

text.p: South Korean corn importers are turning away from the United States and instead seeking corn from Argentina, mainly due to attractive price and quality, traders said on Friday.

"Argentine corn gets more competitiveness in terms of price and quality. It is currently quoted about $10 lower (per tonne) than the U.S. origin," a senior official at the National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) said.
The state-backed NLCF has bought 157,000 tonnes of Argentine feed corn this week, an unusually big purchase from the country in a single week.
"This year, we had purchase deals for two 52,000-tonne cargoes of Argentine corn for arrival on August 9 and September 9," the NLCF official said.
Traders said the NLCF was expected to additionally buy one or two cargoes of Argentine corn early next week.
Leaders of South Korea's major corn buyer groups are currently accompanying President Kim Young-sam on his state visit to South America.
Kim, who is now in Chile, will visit Argentina from September 8-10.
An official at the Korea Corn Processing Industry Association (KOCOPIA) said it had recently bought 55,000 tonnes of Argentine corn that arrived on August 8.

Data from the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry showed that South Korea's corn imports from Argentina totalled only 52,000 tonnes for the first seven months of this year, compared with its overall imports of 5.2 million tonnes.
Imports from Argentina were 26,000 tonnes in all of 1995.
South Korea imported a total of 8.88 million tonnes during the year to October 31, 1995, and the United States supplied 8.62 million tonnes of the total.
Figures for Seoul's imports from the United States in calendar 1995 were not available.
